summary: @ornikar/webpack-config preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute 727 KB obfuscated payload
details: The package's `scripts.preinstall` runs `node setup.mjs`, an obfuscator.io-style scrambled dropper (hex-mangled identifiers such as `_0x488df8` and per-scope string-proxy objects like `_0x19328d.TdVzu = "/etc/os-release"`). setup.mjs downloads a Bun runtime archive from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...`, extracts the `bun` binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` against the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB single-line JavaScript file with a rotated string-array decoder (`WV8StW` shift routine over an ~1500-entry array `n7gIxM`) and hex-mangled identifiers. Fetching an alternate language runtime specifically to execute a bundled obfuscated file at install time is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: the payload runs outside Node's interception surface, is not sourced from the package's own shipped code path, and its behavior is deliberately concealed. This fires automatically on `npm install` before any user interaction with the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
